Adjusted tone incorporating SLOOS:
- Baseline from the FOMC/FSR: balanced with a slight dovish lean (strong labor market, moderate growth, sub-2% inflation; ample-reserves operations aimed at implementation, not additional easing; FSR notes elevated valuations and leverage).
- SLOOS overlay: banks tightened standards and other terms for C&I and construction/land development loans; raised credit score thresholds and tightened credit limits; reported weaker demand in construction/land development and parts of consumer credit; and expect tighter standards, reduced risk tolerance, and some deterioration in loan portfolios/collateral values. Some categories/demand remain unchanged, but the net points to tighter private credit conditions.
- Implication: tighter bank credit and cautious bank expectations add a headwind to growth/inflation, reinforcing the Fed’s patience/no-tightening stance and nudging the tone more dovish than the base read, though not signaling imminent easing.
